title: The Forest of Paper
story:
The heavy oak doors creaked shut behind them, sealing out the damp night air. James stood in an entrance hall of impossible scale, his breath catching in his throat. He had never seen stone rise so high. He had never heard silence so deep. He had never felt air that smelled so heavily of dried lavender, old leather, and ink-stained secrets. Barnaby’s soft footsteps echoed on the polished marble floor, guiding James deeper into the quiet heart of the building.

As they walked, James looked up in sheer wonder. Here were columns that rose like the ancient trunks of the Great Canopy. Here were galleries that curved like the winding boughs of his childhood home. Here were shelves that stretched into the shadows, holding thousands of quiet lives bound in cloth and thread. It felt less like a building of stone and more like a vast, intellectual forest, frozen in time and waiting for a curious traveler to wander its paths.

Barnaby led James into the central rotunda, where a single green-shaded brass lamp illuminated a massive wooden table. In the center of the table sat a giant, rotating sphere made of painted brass and parchment—a terrestrial globe of the entire known world. This man gave the globe a gentle nudge, and it spun silently on its axis, a blur of painted blue oceans and golden landmasses.

James approached the edge of the table, his small fingers reaching out to touch the cold metal ring of the meridian. He held his smooth green sea-glass up to his eye and looked through it at the spinning globe, watching the painted continents warp and glow in the soft emerald light. Somewhere on this vast, spinning ball was his forest, somewhere was this town, and somewhere, waiting in the unpainted margins, was whatever came next.
location: The rotunda of the Grand Library
